definitions.explanation: A formal telegram sent to offer congratulations, typically for weddings, promotions, or other celebrations. Still used in Japan for ceremonial occasions even in the digital age.

examples.japanese: {祝電|しゅくでん}を{送|おく}る。
{結婚式|けっこんしき}に{祝電|しゅくでん}が{届|とど}いた。
examples.english: A congratulatory telegram arrived for the wedding.

examples.japanese: {出席|しゅっせき}できない{代|か}わりに、{祝電|しゅくでん}を{打|う}つことにした。
examples.english: Instead of attending, I decided to send a congratulatory telegram.

notes:
Composed of {祝|しゅく} (celebration) + {電|でん} (telegram). Although telegrams have largely disappeared from daily life, {祝電|しゅくでん} remain a living tradition in Japan, especially at weddings and school ceremonies.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {祝電|しゅくでん}を{送|おく}る: to send a congratulatory telegram
- {祝電|しゅくでん}を{打|う}つ: to send a telegram (lit. "strike")
- {祝電|しゅくでん}が{届|とど}く: a congratulatory telegram arrives
- {祝電|しゅくでん}を{読|よ}み{上|あ}げる: to read aloud a congratulatory telegram

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {弔電|ちょうでん}: condolence telegram — sent for funerals, the opposite occasion
- {電報|でんぽう}: telegram — the general word for any telegram
- {祝辞|しゅくじ}: congratulatory speech — spoken rather than written
